subject: E2E performance qualification — follow-up questions and acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: E2E performance qualification — follow-up questions and acceptance checklist

Hi Samantha — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap plus a short list of technical clarifications we need to validate hosted vs your current provider for final acceptance. Goal: confirm whether Redwood hosted can meet Veridian's end-to-end latency SLOs under realistic traffic and streaming conditions.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary SLOs: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms (end-to-end, app -> Redwood hosted -> model -> response)
- Target concurrency/peak: steady 60 RPS per region, burst to 180 RPS for short windows (~2–3 minutes)
- Typical request shape: 30% streaming calls (inbound streaming + server-side token streaming), 70% single-shot generation; median prompt length ~220 tokens, average response 180 tokens
- Critical gating items: KV/prefix cache warmup behavior, cold-start percentiles, and TLS termination locality.

Attachments: I attached a short checklist and a spreadsheet with the numbers you provided. Please confirm if any of the values below are incorrect or incomplete.

Questions / asks (actionable):
1) Can you share a Flow/Prod example that includes an average request inter-arrival distribution (CSV ok) and a 1-hour spike trace (timestamps + request type)? This lets us replay realistic concurrency.
2) Are there hard requirements for tail latency on streaming responses (e.g., max duration between streamed token batches)? We saw "smooth streaming" was important to UX.
3) What procurement timeline should we align the POC acceptance window to? (30/60/90 days)
4) Any dedicated-region constraints (must-stay-us-east-1 vs multi-region)?

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood runs a 72-hour hosted qualification run using your trace (we request the CSV), producing p50/p95/p99 numbers for both cold and warmed states and separate metrics for streaming vs non-streaming.
- A short SLA acceptance checklist we will fill together (see attached PDF).
- Sync: Tue 11/24 10:00 PT for acceptance criteria sign-off (happy to move).

If that all looks good I'll follow up with a signed NDA/procurement contact to get the trace and a small test token.

Thanks again —
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: veridian_slo_targets.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-hosted-latency-checklist.pdf (pdf, 18KB)]

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veridian.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: E2E performance qualification — follow-up questions and acceptance checklist

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95/p99 numbers are indeed end-to-end as measured at our ingress proxy (post-auth, pre-client). p95 target is aggressive but achievable; p99 is our true concern during burst windows.
- We can share a 24-hour production trace and a separate 10-minute spike trace. I'll put the files on a secure share and send the link to procurement.
- Streaming UX: we require at least one partial token within 200ms of generation start for streaming calls, and subsequent token batches no more than 120ms apart on average. If a batch is delayed more than 500ms we consider it a failure for the UX gating.
- Region: must initially be in us-east-1. Multi-region later is fine but not allowed for this POC.
- Procurement target: 45-day POC + 15-day acceptance window; procurement will push contracts only after acceptance.

I'll have the trace share and procurement contact details by Monday. Also copying Mark (prod infra) separately in a different thread for network details.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Product
Veridian AI

Quick internal note after seeing Samantha's streaming constraints and region requirement:

- Region lock to us-east-1 simplifies the routing test but increases local load; we should size the 72-hour run for steady 60 RPS with bursts to 200 RPS to be conservative.
- Streaming gating: the requirement "first partial token <= 200ms" maps to model decode latency + network. For hosted qualification we should instrument at both ingress (edge -> host) and egress (host -> edge) to attribute time.
- Action items for the POC run:
  * Karthik: build the replay harness that accepts the CSV and replays inter-arrival times + marks streaming vs non-streaming. Include a warm-up period (15 mins) and cold-start windows (simulated infra scale-ups). ETA: Wed 11/25 EOD.
  * Monica: prepare the monitoring dashboard (token-level latency, per-conn streaming gap histogram, p50/p95/p99 per minute). ETA: Thu 11/26 AM.
  * Jasmine: get the trace and procurement contact; schedule the 11/24 sync only if procurement can share the trace.

I'll also prepare a short test plan with the exact metric definitions we will publish (how we compute end-to-end p95/p99, what counts as a streaming failure).

-ben
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Samantha and team. Two quick administrative items before we kick off:

1) Procurement: could you send the secure share link to the trace and a point-of-contact for the NDA? We will sign the NDA and then request a temporary token for the POC replay.
2) Acceptance criteria draft (short):
   - POC run must report end-to-end p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 350ms measured at Veridian ingress for a 24-hour warmed period.
   - Streaming: >= 95% of streaming calls must deliver first partial token <= 200ms and maintain average inter-batch <= 120ms; no more than 1% of streaming calls may have >500ms inter-batch delay.
   - Concurrency: Redwood hosted must sustain steady 60 RPS with verified bursts to 180–200 RPS without violating SLOs for >95% of requests.
   - Cold-start: document and quantify any cold-start p99 windows during the 72-hour run.

If procurement and trace are ready we'll start the replay harness by Wed and hand over the initial results in ~72 hours after the run starts. Scheduling: Tue 11/24 10:00 PT still work for a 30-min alignment?

I'll also attach the brief test plan and the checklist into HubSpot.

Cheers,
